blocks.title: Breathing
blocks.md: We breathe in air through the **nose or mouth**. It goes down the **windpipe** into the **lungs**. In the lungs **oxygen** passes into the **blood** and **carbon dioxide** (a waste gas) passes out, so we breathe out air with more carbon dioxide. About one-fifth of the air is oxygen.

blocks.caption: How oxygen reaches the blood.
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: nose or mouth, windpipe, lungs, blood.

blocks.title: Circulation
blocks.md: The **heart** is a muscle about the size of your fist. It **pumps blood** round the body through tubes called **blood vessels**. Blood carries **oxygen and food** to every part and takes away waste. You can feel the heart beat as your **pulse** at the wrist or neck. Exercise makes the heart beat faster. A resting adult has roughly 60 to 100 beats a minute.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that the lungs make oxygen: they take it from the air.
- Thinking that the heart is on the left side only: it is in the middle of the chest, slightly to the left.
- Counting pulse for too short a time: count for 15 seconds and multiply by 4.
- Thinking that smoke is harmless: tobacco smoke damages the lungs.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Ako counts 18 pulse beats in 15 seconds. How many beats per minute is that?
steps: There are four 15-second periods in a minute.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Why does your heart beat faster after running?
steps: Your muscles need more oxygen and food when you run.
The heart pumps faster to carry more blood to them.
blocks.answer: The muscles need more oxygen, so the heart pumps faster.

blocks.title: A healthy diet
blocks.md: We need **carbohydrates** for energy (cassava, rice, yam), **proteins** for growth and repair (beans, fish, eggs), **vitamins and minerals** for health (fruit, vegetables), a little **fat** and **plenty of water**. Eating too little protein or too few fruits and vegetables for a long time can cause **deficiency diseases**. A **balanced diet** has all groups in the right amounts.

blocks.title: Why food goes bad
blocks.md: Food goes bad when **germs** such as **bacteria and moulds** grow on it. They grow best in **warm, wet** conditions. Bad food can cause stomach pains, diarrhoea and vomiting. We **preserve** food by removing water, adding salt or smoke, cooling, or sealing it in tins.

blocks.caption: Ways of keeping food safe.
blocks.alt: A table of preservation methods: drying removes water, smoking, salting draws out water, cooling slows germs and canning seals food; examples are dried fish, smoked fish, salted fish, fridge and tinned tomatoes.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Eating food that smells bad because it still looks fine.
- Leaving cooked food in the heat for hours.
- Keeping raw and cooked food together.
- Thinking that a food kept in the fridge never goes bad: it only lasts longer.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Why is fish smoked or dried in many villages?
steps: Smoking and drying remove water, and germs cannot grow without water.
So the fish can be kept for days or weeks.
blocks.answer: It removes water, so germs cannot grow and the fish keeps longer.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Why should cooked food be covered?
steps: Flies carry germs from dirty places.
Covering keeps flies and dust away.
blocks.answer: To keep flies and germs off the food.

blocks.title: Germs and disease
blocks.md: **Germs** are tiny living things (bacteria, viruses and other parasites) that can make us ill. They spread through **dirty water and food**, the **air** (coughs and sneezes), **touching** and **insect bites**. **Malaria** is spread by mosquitoes; **cholera and typhoid** by dirty water and food; the **common cold** by coughs and sneezes.

blocks.caption: Some diseases and how to prevent them.
blocks.alt: A table with four diseases: malaria spread by mosquito bite; cholera spread by dirty water and food; typhoid spread by dirty food or water; the common cold spread by germs in the air, with the prevention of each.

blocks.title: Prevention
blocks.md: **Wash hands** with soap, drink **safe water**, **cover coughs**, use a **toilet or latrine** and keep it clean, sleep under a **mosquito net**, remove **stagnant water**, and keep **vaccination** appointments (vaccines protect against several diseases, as advised by health workers). A healthy diet and sleep help the body to fight germs.

blocks.title: Basic first aid
blocks.md: For a **small cut**: wash your hands, rinse the cut with clean water and cover it with a clean cloth or plaster. For a **burn**: put the burnt area under **cool running water** for a few minutes; do not put oil or toothpaste on it. For anything serious (heavy bleeding, a broken bone, a bad burn, a snake bite) **call an adult and take the person to a health centre at once**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that diseases are caused by a curse or by the weather alone.
- Treating a serious injury at home instead of going to a health worker.
- Sharing cups and plates with a sick person.
- Stopping a vaccination programme because the child feels well.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A family has diarrhoea after drinking water from a stream. What is the likely cause and what should they do?
steps: Stream water may carry germs such as those of cholera or typhoid.
They should go to a health centre and, in future, boil, filter or treat the water.
blocks.answer: Germs in the unsafe water; seek health care and use only safe water.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name two ways of preventing malaria.
steps: Mosquitoes carry malaria, so keep them away from people.
Sleep under a net and remove stagnant water.
blocks.answer: Sleep under a mosquito net; remove stagnant water.
